question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Early Portuguese trade ports in India]
options: Cochin (Kochi) – first Portuguese-friendly port used as ally against the Zamorin
Cannanore (Kannur) – northern Kerala port where Portuguese had early friendly relations
Quilon (Kollam) – southernmost major port that traded with Portuguese ships
Daman – the port where Vasco da Gama signed the first Portuguese-Indian trade treaty in 1498
wrong_fact: Vasco da Gama did NOT sign a trade treaty at Daman. He landed at Calicut (not Daman) in 1498, and no formal treaty was signed. Daman was a Portuguese possession much later (captured 1535) and played no role in da Gama's first voyage.
explanation: In 1498, Vasco da Gama anchored near Calicut (at Kappakadavu/Kappad) and met the Zamorin but left without a formal treaty. The early Portuguese-friendly ports were Cochin and Cannanore, whose rulers saw an advantage in allying with the Portuguese against the dominant Zamorin. Quilon (Kollam) on the southern Kerala coast was another significant port. Daman was a Portuguese territorial acquisition only in 1535, nearly four decades after da Gama's first voyage.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Pre-Portuguese Indian Ocean trade routes]
options: Calicut to Aden – major Arab dhow route carrying Malabar spices to the Red Sea
Calicut to Hormuz – route carrying spices into the Persian Gulf for overland distribution
Malabar spices reached Venice via – Egypt and the Mediterranean Sea
The main competitors of Arab traders in the Indian Ocean before 1498 were – Portuguese caravels that regularly traded at Calicut
wrong_fact: Portuguese caravels did NOT regularly trade at Calicut before 1498 – Vasco da Gama's voyage WAS the first Portuguese arrival in India. Before 1498, Arab, Indian (especially Gujarati), and Chinese merchants dominated Indian Ocean trade. Portugal had no presence east of the Cape of Good Hope before da Gama's voyage.
explanation: Before 1498, the Indian Ocean spice trade was dominated by Arab merchants (carrying goods to Aden/Hormuz), Gujarati Muslim traders, and smaller South Asian coastal traders. Malabar spices flowed via Aden to Egypt (Red Sea), then overland or via Venice to Europe. The Chinese had withdrawn from active Indian Ocean trade after Zheng He's voyages (ended ~1433). Portugal's entrance in 1498 was entirely new – they had no prior presence in the Indian Ocean, which is precisely what made da Gama's voyage so momentous.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Portuguese factories and trading posts – early phase 1498–1510]
options: First Portuguese factory in India established at – Calicut (by Cabral, 1500, later destroyed)
Portuguese allied port of Cochin – gave them a base to stockpile spices after Calicut factory fell
Cannanore (Kannur) factory – established around 1502, remained relatively stable for Portuguese
The factory at Goa – established by Vasco da Gama in 1498 as the primary base for all three voyages
wrong_fact: Vasco da Gama did NOT establish a factory at Goa in 1498. Goa was captured by Afonso de Albuquerque in 1510 – twelve years after da Gama's first voyage. Da Gama's first voyage did not visit Goa at all as a trading base.
explanation: The chronology of Portuguese factories in India: Calicut factory (1500, by Cabral) was destroyed. Cochin became the first stable base (~1500–1503). Cannanore factory (~1502) was relatively peaceful. Goa was captured only in 1510 by Albuquerque and became the capital of Estado da India. During Vasco da Gama's first voyage (1498), no permanent factory was established anywhere – the Portuguese were still explorers finding their way. Goa's rise as the Portuguese headquarters came over a decade later.
